newsitem.title: USA: Demand, production problems push U.S. MTBE higher.
newsitem.headline: Demand, production problems push U.S. MTBE higher.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices rose about a half cent in the U.S. Gulf as supplies cinched tighter amid more production problems and demand, players said Wednesday.

The latest glitch in production cutbacks was ARCO Chemical's 20,000 barrel-per-day plant in Rotterdam, which is shutting down for four to five days for an unscheduled maintenance, a company source said.
The plant recently returned online from a scheduled turnaround and is a larg exporter of the gasoline additive to the U.S.
There was also talk Enron's 17,000 bpd Morgan's Point facility went down on Friday but it could not be immediately confirmed.
"Production problems still prevail. Supply is almost non-existent in the Gulf," said a Houston MTBE trader.
Players said a prompt 93.00-cent deal in the U.S. Gulf Coast was done on Tuesday, and a parcel as high as 94.00 cents was heard done but could not be confirmed.
On the East Coast, New York Harbor prompt barrels remained 97.00/98.00 cents.
In addition, demand has remained strong by blenders, who have been buying hand-to-mouth for use in their pool of reformulated gasoline.
"There is true end-use demand out there. It is not speculators," said a Gulf trader.
Meanwhile, the spread between conventional unleaded and regular reformulated gasoline has blown out from the traditional 1.00 cents to 1.50 cents to about 4.00 cents in the Gulf.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk 1212 859-1631--
